info.description: Admin API of the goose proxy-pool engine: create and manage inbounds (http/socks5 listeners), outbounds (proxy plugins), pools and chains, and inspect request metrics.
info.title: goose admin API

get.description:
Returns all configured proxy chains (ordered lists of pool layers).
Returns the chain with the given id.
Creates (or replaces) a proxy chain: an ordered list of layers, each referencing a pool (which carries its own filters + selector) or a single outbound server (pinned for that hop; when an id matches both, the pool wins). Layer 0 is the first hop; each subsequent layer is dialed through the previous.
Removes the chain with the given id. Inbounds whose policy still references it will fail to resolve until reconfigured.

get.description: Returns the latest auto-chain reachability verdict per probed outbound: whether the engine can dial the member's server directly and, when it cannot, whether an access-pool proxy can relay to it (and which one). Members whose server is unreachable both ways are dropped from routing; members reachable only via relay are routed through that relay (auto-built chain).
get.summary: List reachability probes for access-filtered pool members

get.description: Returns the engine-level configuration: network stack selection, admin API settings, metrics DB path and offline geo database settings.

Returns up to n recent exit-IP check records, newest first: for each checked outbound, the site it was asked, the public IP observed at the proxy's exit, latency, and time. Optionally filtered to one outbound. A proxy's connect address is not its exit address, and the exit can vary by site and over time — history makes both visible. Scheduling is configured on the engine resource (exit_checks.enabled / cron / interval_seconds / sites / timeout_seconds / concurrency).

parameters.description: Number of records to return (default 100, max 10000)
parameters.name: n

post.description: Starts one exit-IP check round immediately (background); results appear in GET /api/exit-checks as they complete. Uses the engine's exit-check site list, timeout, and concurrency. Scheduling (cron/interval) is unaffected.
post.summary: Trigger an exit-IP check round now

get.description:
Returns all configured inbound listeners.
Returns the inbound listener with the given id.
Creates (or replaces) an inbound listener. When the body carries no id, the id must be supplied in the URL path (/api/inbounds/{id}); when both are present they must match. The policy routes the inbound (or, via per-user policy overrides, each user) to a named chain (chain_id), one pinned outbound server (outbound_id), or a single pool (pool_id, optionally narrowed by filters) — in that order of preference; when none is set, any available outbound. A user policy that sets any route field replaces the inbound's route as a group, and user filters are the user's own (replacing the inbound-level ones). Filters narrow every layer of a named chain too. Changes apply live: the engine starts/stops listeners on the next config version bump.
Removes the inbound listener with the given id and stops it.

get.description:
Returns all configured dynamic outbound providers. Each provider feeds one or more managed pools (pool_ids) with the outbounds it fetches; providers created without a pool_ids list report the default pool "default".
Returns the provider spec with the given id.
Creates (or replaces) a dynamic outbound provider. The provider names a registered provider plugin (e.g. "psiphon", "subscription", "mihomo", "singbox"); pool_ids lists the managed pools its outbounds are merged into — every pool in the list receives the provider's full outbound set — and defaults to ["default"] when omitted (the legacy singular pool_id is still accepted as a one-entry list); config is plugin-specific. Changes apply live: the engine starts, restarts, or stops the provider's poll loop on the next config version bump.
Removes the provider with the given id, stops its poll loop, and drops its managed outbounds and every pool it exclusively fed.

parameters.description: Provider id (ignored unless the body omits it)
parameters.name: id

error.description: Error is a short, human-readable reason for the rejection.

token.description: Token is the bearer token for admin auth; empty disables auth.

access_pool_id.description:
AccessPoolID is the pool of access (relay) proxies used to reach
members whose servers the local network cannot dial directly (e.g.
proxies behind an ISP block). Required; must reference an existing pool.

probe_interval_seconds.description:
ProbeIntervalSec is seconds between reachability probe rounds.
Default 300; minimum 10.

probe_timeout_seconds.description: ProbeTimeoutSec bounds each probe dial. Default 5; minimum 1.

layers.description: pool or outbound IDs, in order

api.description: API is the admin server config.

db.description: DB is the metrics database path.

exit_checks.description:
ExitChecks configures scheduled exit-IP checks: the engine dials each
outbound and asks an "what is my IP" style site for the exit IP,
recording results. Zero value (disabled) keeps the engine from making
any unsolicited outbound requests.

geo.description: Geo is the offline IP database config.

stack.description: Stack selects the network stack: "system" or "gvisor".

concurrency.description:
Concurrency caps parallel checks in one round, protecting the check
sites (and their rate limits) from a burst. Default 4; minimum 1.

cron.description:
Cron is a 5-field crontab expression (min hour dom mon dow) for the
check schedule. When set it takes precedence over IntervalSec.

enabled.description: Enabled turns scheduled checks on. Default false.

interval_seconds.description: IntervalSec is seconds between check rounds, used when Cron is empty.

sites.description:
Sites are exit-IP check URLs that respond with the caller's IP as
plain text (e.g. https://ifconfig.me). Checks rotate round-robin
across this list so large batches spread load instead of tripping one
site's rate limits. Empty selects the built-in defaults.

timeout_seconds.description: TimeoutSec bounds each check. Default 15; minimum 1.

path.description: Path is the database file path.

chain_id.description: ChainID references a Chain in the chain store.

filters.description:
Filters narrow the route's candidates for this inbound or user only
(same FilterSpec shape as a pool's filters). With pool routing they
apply on top of the pool's own filters; with chain routing they narrow
every layer's pool. A user's filters replace the inbound-level ones.

outbound_id.description:
OutboundID references one Outbound to route through directly,
pinning this inbound (or user) to a single server. Takes precedence
over PoolID, but not over ChainID.

pool_id.description:
PoolID references a Pool to route through directly, without needing a
named chain. Ignored when ChainID or OutboundID is set.

upstream_proxy.description:
UpstreamProxy routes this outbound's own connection to its proxy
server through an engine-managed route instead of dialing it directly
from the engine host. Empty (the default) keeps the pre-existing
behavior: the server connection rides the engine stack alone. The
reference forms are the same ones ProviderSpec.UpstreamProxy accepts
(outbound:<id>, pool:<id>, chain:<id>, a bare id, or "direct"), minus
"access" — that form resolves the access pool of the pools a
*provider* feeds, and a static outbound feeds none. The engine
resolves the reference at dial time against live config and injects
the dialer into the plugin's config map under
pkg/plugin.UpstreamDialerKey; outbound plugins that support an
upstream (http, socks5, mihomo-*, singbox-*) reach their server
through it, composing with the engine stack: the route's own first
hop dials through the engine's system/gvisor stack.

access.description:
Access, when set, turns the pool into an auto-chained pool: the engine
probes each member's server for direct reachability from the local
network; members the local ISP cannot reach are dialed through an
access proxy from Access.AccessPoolID (a relay hop is prepended
automatically), and members reachable neither directly nor through the
access pool are dropped from the pool's candidates.

config.description: Config is the plugin-specific provider configuration.

pool_ids.description: PoolIDs are the managed pools to populate; empty means the default pool.

upstream_proxy.description:
UpstreamProxy routes the provider's own URL fetches (subscription
download, server-list fetch, ...) through an engine-managed route
instead of dialing directly from the engine host. Empty (the default)
keeps direct fetches. The reference is one of:

  - "outbound:<id>":  one specific proxy server (a configured outbound);
    a bare id is also accepted — resolved as a pool when a pool with
    that id exists, else as an outbound (same precedence as chain
    layers), so "pool:<id>" and "outbound:<id>" pin the meaning
  - "pool:<id>":      pick an outbound from a pool (its selector, with
    failover across members; the pool's access filter applies, so
    members the local network cannot reach are dialed through the
    pool's access proxies)
  - "chain:<id>":     traverse a named chain layer by layer (real
    multi-hop semantics: hop i CONNECTs toward hop i+1's server, the
    last hop toward the fetch target)
  - "access":         dial the fetch target directly first, and fall
    back to the access pool of the pools this provider feeds (the
    same direct-vs-relay testing the access filter does for pool
    members) when the local network cannot reach it
  - "direct":         always dial directly (explicit no-op form)

The engine resolves the reference at dial time against live config, so
pool membership and access-pool changes apply without restarting the
provider; editing the reference itself restarts it. The resolved dialer
is injected into the provider's config map for plugins that support
routed fetches (see pkg/plugin.UpstreamDialer).

params.description: Params is strategy-specific config, e.g. sticky: {"key":"domain"}.

policy.description:
Policy overrides the inbound-level policy for this user. Route fields
(chain_id / outbound_id / pool_id) are replaced as a group when the
user policy sets any of them, otherwise the inbound's route is
inherited. Filters are the user's own: when present they replace the
inbound-level filters, so each user can be narrowed independently.

site.description:
Site is the host of the check site that was asked (e.g.
"ifconfig.me").

at.description: At is when the probe ran.

error.description: Error is the dial error when OK is false.

latency.description: Latency is how long the dial took.

ok.description: OK reports whether the dial succeeded.

details.description:
Details carries plugin-specific live facts (counts, addresses,
timestamps). Keys are the plugin's own; the UI renders them as-is.

message.description:
Message is one line of context for the state, e.g. the last error or
a progress note. Empty means "nothing to say".

state.description:
State is a short, human-readable phase word, e.g. "running",
"establishing", "error". Plugins pick their own vocabulary; the
engine surfaces it verbatim.

id.description: ID is the provider spec ID.

last_ok_at.description: LastOKAt is when Outbounds last succeeded.

last_poll_at.description: LastPollAt is when Outbounds was last called, successfully or not.

message.description: Message carries the last Outbounds error when State is "error".

outbound_count.description: OutboundCount is the last successful poll's outbound count.

plugin.description:
Plugin holds the provider's own self-assessment, when it implements
pub.StatusReporter. Nil (and omitted from JSON) when it does not.

pools.description: Pools lists the pool IDs the provider feeds.

provider.description: Provider is the plugin name, e.g. "psiphon".

started_at.description: StartedAt is when the provider instance was instantiated.

state.description:
State is the engine's phase word: "running" (goroutine alive, last
poll succeeded), "error" (last poll failed — pools kept stale), or
"starting" (instantiated but not yet polled).
